latest.content:

THIS ANNOUNCEMENT CONTAINS INSIDE INFORMATION FOR THE PURPOSES OF ARTICLE 7 OF REGULATION 596/2014 AS AMENDED AND TRANSPOSED INTO UK LAW IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE EUROPEAN UNION (WITHDRAWAL) ACT 2018 ("UK MAR").
6 July 2026
Seascape Energy Asia plc
("Seascape Energy", the "Company" or "Seascape")
Leave of Absence and Interim Appointment
Seascape Energy, an E&P company focused on Southeast Asia, has been informed that its Executive Chairman, James Menzies, will be taking a medical leave-of-absence for an initial three-month period following a cycling accident.
Geraldine Murphy, currently Senior Independent Director, has been appointed Interim Non-Executive Chair with immediate effect. There are no other changes to board roles at this time.
Geraldine has over 35 years of energy investment banking and M&A experience in senior roles at Standard Chartered Bank, Harrison Lovegrove, CIBC and Perella Weinberg Partners. Geraldine joined the Seascape board in June 2024 and has been instrumental in the transformational pivot of the Company to Southeast Asia and subsequent growth initiatives.
In addition to her role at Seascape, Geraldine is also an Independent Non-Executive Director at Ithaca Energy plc, a FTSE 250 E&P business focused on the UK Continental Shelf. Geraldine holds a BSc (Hons) degree in Geology and a MSc in Petroleum Geology from University College Dublin.
Geraldine Murphy, Interim Non-Executive Chair, commented:
"Our thoughts are with James and his family and we wish him a full and speedy recovery. I look forward to continuing to work closely with the Seascape executive team to deliver the significant value in our Malaysian portfolio recently highlighted at our AGM."
Ends

latest.title: Mandate to Structure and Arrange Debt Finance
latest.content:
25 Jun 2026 07:10
RNS Number : 6588J
Seascape Energy Asia PLC
25 June 2026
THIS ANNOUNCEMENT CONTAINS INSIDE INFORMATION FOR THE PURPOSES OF ARTICLE 7 OF REGULATION 596/2014 AS AMENDED AND TRANSPOSED INTO UK LAW IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE EUROPEAN UNION (WITHDRAWAL) ACT 2018 ("UK MAR").
25 June 2026
Seascape Energy Asia plc
(the "Company", "Seascape Energy" or "Seascape")
Mandate to Structure and Arrange Debt Finance Facilities
Seascape Energy, an E&P company focused on Southeast Asia, is pleased to announce that it has exclusively mandated Macquarie Bank Limited ("Macquarie") to act as the sole Structuring Bank and Technical and Modelling Bank for the debt financing to support the development of the DEWA Cluster (SEA 28%) and Temaris Cluster (SEA 100%) gas fields, offshore Malaysia.
Seascape will work together with Macquarie over the coming months to structure and execute a multi-tranche, debt facility to meet development expenditure with availability linked to certain milestones typical for this type of financing. Any firm offer of financing remains subject to the successful completion of legal and technical due diligence and Macquarie's receipt of all required internal approvals.
Nick Ingrassia
, CEO of Seascape, commented:
"Macquarie Bank has a long history of deploying capital to support growth-focused E&P companies like Seascape. We are extremely pleased they have committed to work with us to secure financing to develop these important gas projects to secure domestic supply into Malaysia and regional export markets."
Ends

company_30s.what_they_do: Seascape Energy Ltd. is a small‑cap oil and gas exploration firm focused on developing hydrocarbon prospects in the UK and offshore Europe. It acquires, drills, and sells exploration licences, and its core product is the sale of discovered reserves to larger operators.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The company sits in a niche of early‑stage exploration where a single successful discovery can unlock significant value. Its assets are in a region with growing demand for energy resources, and it has a track record of securing development agreements that can turn a discovery into a revenue‑generating asset.
company_30s.current_state: Seascape is in a restructuring phase, having recently announced a board reshuffle, a planned debt refinancing, and an equity raise to shore up its balance sheet. The firm is still in the exploration stage, burning cash to keep rigs on standby and to negotiate development deals.

rns_narrative: The company has been busy shuffling its board and securing financing. A 2026 AGM revealed a new interim CEO and a plan to raise debt and equity to fund future drilling. The management team is also pushing for a partnership to develop the Kertang Prospect, which could provide a clear exit route if the field is productive.

Second theme: Operational updates. Seascape is reporting progress on its offshore licences and has just filed a wrap retail offer that was oversubscribed, indicating investor appetite for the next round of capital.

Third theme: Governance and risk management. The firm is addressing a deferred bonus payout and a leave of absence for a senior executive, signalling a focus on stabilising leadership and aligning incentives.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Bullish optimism but cautious about execution
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Traders are excited about the potential upside from a successful Kertang development and the recent oversubscription of the equity offer. They see Seascape as a value play that could jump once a development agreement is signed.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Concerns centre on the company’s heavy cash burn and the fact that it has yet to produce a commercial field. A failure to secure a development partner could leave the firm with a large debt burden and no clear path to profitability.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The community has shifted from silent to active discussion after the AGM and the equity offer. Sentiment has become more optimistic, but many still warn that the next big move will come only if a development deal is finalised.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends are flat, indicating no public awareness. This silence means a news catalyst could catch the market off‑guard, creating a sharp rebound.

near_term_catalysts: A signed development agreement for the Kertang Prospect – a partnership that would bring in a large upfront payment and a revenue stream.
Completion of the equity raise by Q3 2026, which would improve liquidity and give the company breathing room to drill.
Positive drilling results from a recently acquired licence, which could validate the geological model and trigger a confidence spike.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden spike in trading volume (at least 3× average) that coincides with a positive press release or a signed deal. Monitor the company’s debt schedule; if the debt refinancing is executed without new equity, that could signal a liquidity crunch.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early to mid‑stage of a deep crash cycle – the price has fallen past 80% of its peak and volume has thinned. A mean‑reversion play will likely need a catalyst that confirms the company’s operational viability before the market starts to re‑price.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The deep crash has left the share price very cheap compared to the company’s asset base. If a development deal materialises, the price could rebound to the mid‑crash level, giving a 4‑5× return on the current price. The historical record for RED‑colour signals shows an average 160% upside, so even a modest bounce would be profitable.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the company fails to secure a development partner or the equity raise stalls, it could run out of cash and face forced liquidation. The worst‑case scenario would be a 70% further drop to the 2023 low, which is still above the 86% drawdown threshold but would wipe out the upside.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside is roughly 4–5× the current price, while downside risk is capped at the remaining 30% of the current price. The asymmetry is roughly 4:1, which is attractive for a contrarian position.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a pullback to the 20‑day moving average, with a position size that limits exposure to 5% of the portfolio. Place a stop just below the recent swing low to protect against a false breakout. Use a target at the 50‑day high from the last swing, which aligns with the 4× upside.
playbook.if_watching: Hold a small protective position until a development agreement is announced or the equity offer is fully subscribed. Watch for volume spikes above 3× the 10‑day average as a signal that the market is reacting to positive news.
playbook.if_passing: If the company announces a default on its debt obligations or a regulatory ban on its licences, exit immediately.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Seascape’s deep crash, coupled with a pending development deal and an oversubscribed equity raise, creates a high‑reward contrarian play with a clear upside target and a well‑defined downside ceiling.
